fusrap-usace-iowa-army-aap.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remedial action underway. ROD completed 2011 (excavation and sorting of depleted-uranium-contaminated soil with off-site disposal, and building decontamination). As of the June 2025 Stakeholder Report, remediation activities were ongoing and USACE had completed the second Five-Year Review and updated the community involvement plan. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Depleted uranium (DU-contaminated soil and building contamination from AEC weapons-assembly operations, 1947–1975, on 1,630 acres of the plant)

fusrap-usace-joslyn-manufacturing-supply.st: investigation complete, proposed plan in preparation
fusrap-usace-joslyn-manufacturing-supply.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — investigation complete, proposed plan in preparation. Official USACE Buffalo District page (updated Oct. 20, 2025): PA August 2005, SI May 2007, RI initiated March 2020. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: RI report completed in 2024 and concluded that buildings and environmental materials on-site do not pose a risk to human health or the environment; USACE will prepare a proposed plan recommending no remedial action. A Dec. 4, 2025 USACE Buffalo District release provided $75,000 to continue preparation of the proposed plan. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Natural uranium (tempering, hot rolling, quenching, straightening, cooling, grinding, cutting, and threading of natural uranium billets into metal rods)

fusrap-usace-w-r-grace-curtis-bay-site.n: W.R. Grace at Curtis Bay Site
fusrap-usace-w-r-grace-curtis-bay-site.st: Building 23 remedial action underway; Radioactive Waste Disposal Area remedial action not yet started
fusrap-usace-w-r-grace-curtis-bay-site.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — Building 23 remedial action underway; Radioactive Waste Disposal Area remedial action not yet started. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: Building 23 RI 2002, FS 2003, Proposed Plan 2004; ROD issued 2005 and amended 2020 (remedy changed from decontamination to demolition, plus land-use controls for soil); RA for Building 23 is ongoing; first Five-Year Review for Building 23 issued 2021. RWDA revised final RI 2001, FS 2009, Proposed Plan 2009, ROD 2011 (excavation, segregation, and off-site disposal, with potential land-use controls); RWDA remedial action is planned after Building 23. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants

Thorium and rare-earth elements extracted from monazite sand (May 1956 through early 1957) in the southwest quadrant of Building 23; processing wastes disposed on-site in the Radioactive Waste Disposal Area

fusrap-usace-latty-avenue-properties.st: remediation complete; close-out and institutional controls in preparation
fusrap-usace-latty-avenue-properties.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remediation complete; close-out and institutional controls in preparation. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: remediation has been completed; one property will require ICs and the remainder will be released for unrestricted use; groundwater monitoring will be required; USACE is drafting the site close-out report and preparing the Missouri Environmental Covenant for implementation of ICs. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM; not a completed/transferred LM site.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium-ore processing residues (hauled from the St. Louis Airport Site), which contaminated soil, groundwater, and building surfaces

fusrap-usace-st-louis-airport-site.st: site remediation complete (2007); property still used to support vicinity-property work and has not transferred to DOE LM
fusrap-usace-st-louis-airport-site.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — site remediation complete (2007); property still used to support vicinity-property work and has not transferred to DOE LM. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: 21-acre site just north of the St. Louis Airport; added to the NPL on Oct. 4, 1989 (MOD980633176); USACE completed remediation in 2007 in accordance with the ROD; the site is currently used as the loadout area for soils remediated at the SLAPS Vicinity Properties. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM; not a completed/transferred LM site.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium-processing residues and other material from the St. Louis Downtown Site (Mallinckrodt), stored at SLAPS beginning in 1946; adjacent properties were contaminated by erosion and spillage

fusrap-usace-st-louis-airport-site-vicin.n: St. Louis Airport Site Vicinity Properties
fusrap-usace-st-louis-airport-site-vicin.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — soil remediation ongoing. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: more than 148 properties in the cities of Hazelwood and Berkeley, including 14.2 miles of the Coldwater Creek corridor from Banshee Road to the Missouri River, adjacent ball fields, railroad property, roads and ditches, airport-authority property, and haul routes; in 2024 USACE completed initial investigative sampling along 14.2 miles of Coldwater Creek; soil remediation activities are ongoing. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Low-level radioactive contamination (uranium-bearing residues) linked to both SLAPS and the Latty Avenue Properties, including soils and sediments of vicinity properties and Coldwater Creek

fusrap-usace-st-louis-downtown-site.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remedial action underway. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: St. Louis District continues remedial activities under the 1998 Record of Decision for accessible areas, which includes the Mallinckrodt plant and 42 known vicinity properties; the 2014 ROD for the Group 1 Inaccessible Soils Operable Unit selected no further action; Group 2 Inaccessible Soils were being evaluated; soil remediation activities are ongoing. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium compounds and uranium metal (processing, machining, and recovery of uranium under MED/AEC contract, 1942–1957)

fusrap-usace-dupont-chambers-works.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remedial action underway. ROD signed 2013 (excavation of radiologically impacted soil and monitored natural attenuation of groundwater). USACE issued an Explanation of Significant Differences in 2024 after identifying additional radiologically contaminated soils not in the 2013 ROD, and continued remediation in 2024. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium (historical MED/AEC uranium-refining; uranium oxide converted to uranium hexafluoride and small quantities of uranium metal)

fusrap-usace-maywood-chemical-superfund-.st: soils largely remediated under the 2003 ROD; inaccessible soils remain; groundwater remedy not yet fully implemented
fusrap-usace-maywood-chemical-superfund-.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — soils largely remediated under the 2003 ROD; inaccessible soils remain; groundwater remedy not yet fully implemented. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: soils at the 11.7-acre government-owned NPL parcel have been remediated to restricted-use standards; vicinity-property soils have been remediated to unrestricted or restricted use based on land use; inaccessible soils remain beneath local roadways, New Jersey Route 17, and Interstate 80 and are remediated as they become accessible; the 2012 groundwater ROD selected in situ treatment, monitored natural attenuation, and groundwater-use restrictions, and groundwater remediation was to be implemented within the next year (from that June 2025 report). Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM. LM is the owner of record at Maywood (SMG March 2026 note) while USACE remains the lead cleanup agency.
fig: Contaminants
Thorium-232 (primary contaminant), from monazite-sand extraction by the former Maywood Chemical Works, 1916–1959

fusrap-usace-middlesex-municipal-landfil.st: soils ROD complete; remedial design in development
fusrap-usace-middlesex-municipal-landfil.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — soils ROD complete; remedial design in development. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: RI/FS completed August 2019; Proposed Plan issued July 2021; soils ROD finalized September 2022 (excavation to unrestricted-use levels); no groundwater contamination detected; USACE is developing the remedial design. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants

Radium-226 and uranium-238 (soil with radioactive contamination originally disposed from the Middlesex Sampling Plant; later surveys identified above-background Ra-226 and U-238 in previously unremediated areas)

fusrap-usace-middlesex-sampling-plant.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — soils remediated; groundwater remediation underway. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: soils ROD issued FY 2005; soil remediation completed 2008; groundwater ROD finalized 2021 (in situ chemical reduction, monitored natural attenuation, and land-use controls); in 2024 USACE completed the review of potential vicinity properties for the Soils Operable Unit and implemented an in-situ chemical reduction pilot study for groundwater. The same report states the site was dispositioned in January 2024; groundwater remediation remains in progress and the site is still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium, thorium, and beryllium ores (and later-stored thorium residues); African uranium ore / pitchblende historically stored and shipped from the site

fusrap-usace-guterl-specialty-steel.st: post-ROD, remediation contract awarded, fieldwork not yet started
fusrap-usace-guterl-specialty-steel.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — post-ROD, remediation contract awarded, fieldwork not yet started. RI completed 2010; FS and Proposed Plan 2021; ROD finalized 2023 and publicly released 2024 (dismantle AEC-era buildings, excavate and dispose contaminated soil, treat uranium groundwater plume). In fall 2026 USACE Buffalo District awarded a contract valued up to $249 million; site work is anticipated to commence in 2027. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium and thorium (foundry and rolling-mill operations on approximately 25 million pounds of uranium metal and 30,000 pounds of thorium metal, 1948–1956)

fusrap-usace-niagara-falls-storage-site.st: Balance of Plant remedial action underway; Interim Waste Containment Structure remains in place
fusrap-usace-niagara-falls-storage-site.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — Balance of Plant remedial action underway; Interim Waste Containment Structure remains in place. Official USACE NFSS page (updated Sept. 9, 2026): 191-acre federally owned site with a 10-acre IWCS; as of August 2026, 101 of 102 Phase I Balance of Plant excavation areas had been completed, with more than 1,600 truckloads / 26,000 cubic yards shipped off-site. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: draft ROD for Balance of Plant and Groundwater OUs in FY 2021; IWCS remedial-design study and open vicinity properties E, E-Prime, G, H-Prime, and X still under investigation or pending access. A Dec. 4, 2025 USACE Buffalo District release provided $3 million for completion of ongoing BOP OU remediation. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants

Radioactive residues, contaminated demolition rubble/debris, and contaminated soil stored in the Interim Waste Containment Structure, plus FUSRAP-eligible soil and groundwater contamination in the Balance of Plant (residues from 1940s–1950s waste brought to the site)

fusrap-usace-seaway-industrial-park-site.st: engineered cap construction complete; long-term monitoring and a Five-Year Review pending
fusrap-usace-seaway-industrial-park-site.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — engineered cap construction complete; long-term monitoring and a Five-Year Review pending. Official USACE Buffalo District release (Feb. 4, 2026, updated Feb. 4, 2026): 2009 ROD remedy is containment with limited off-site disposal; cap of Areas A, B, and C completed December 2025; final seeding scheduled spring 2026; Northside excavation (1,121 cubic yards) completed in FY 2016; Five-Year Review report scheduled for summer 2027. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report had anticipated cap completion in summer of FY 2025 and transfer in 2029; those earlier forecast dates are superseded by the later official USACE release and the March 2026 SMG. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Radium, thorium, uranium, and uranium daughter products (FUSRAP-related material / uranium-processing residues in the landfill and adjacent Northside and Southside areas)

fusrap-usace-staten-island-warehouse.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — time-critical removal action implemented in 2024. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: 1.25-acre site at the base of the Bayonne Bridge on Richmond Terrace Avenue on Staten Island; added to FUSRAP in May 2021; confirmatory sampling in 2021; Action Memorandum in September 2022 documenting a time-critical removal action, implemented in 2024. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
High-grade Belgian Congo uranium ore (historically stored in drums at the warehouse, 1939–1942)

fusrap-usace-sylvania-corning-plant.st: remedial investigation complete; feasibility study under regulatory review
fusrap-usace-sylvania-corning-plant.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remedial investigation complete; feasibility study under regulatory review. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: PA 2005; on-site RI 2010; Congress added the site in 2006; included in a regional groundwater NPL listing in 2011; USACE finalized the RI report in FY 2021; in 2024 USACE submitted a Feasibility Study for regulatory review. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Natural, enriched, and depleted uranium, some thorium, nickel, and tetrachloroethene

fusrap-usace-harshaw-chemical-company.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remedial action underway. RI completed 2009; ROD for OU-1 and OU-2 issued November 2021 (excavation and off-site disposal). Contractors began staging equipment and air monitoring in early May 2024. The June 2025 Stakeholder Report said USACE expected to complete work in summer of FY 2025; a Dec. 4, 2025 USACE Buffalo District release provided $30 million for completion of ongoing site remediation, so work was still underway as of that date. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium (various forms processed in Building G-1 / Plant C, 1944–1959, for isotopic separation and enrichment at Oak Ridge)

fusrap-usace-luckey-site.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — remedial action underway. Soils ROD 2006 (excavation and off-site disposal of soils contaminated with beryllium, lead, radium-226, thorium-230, uranium-234, and uranium-238); groundwater ROD 2008 (monitored natural attenuation). Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: RA began 2017; Phase 1 and 2 soil excavation completed December 2020; Phase 3 building deconstruction completed by September 2021; FY 2024 work centered on excavation and off-site shipment of contaminated materials, with on-site water treatment. Official USACE Luckey page (updated July 16, 2026) reports 93,777 cubic yards excavated from Phase 1 and 2 areas and that a five-year review of the soils and groundwater remedies was in process. A Dec. 4, 2025 USACE Buffalo District release provided $5 million for completion of ongoing site remediation. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants
Beryllium, lead, radium-226, thorium-230, uranium-234, and uranium-238

fusrap-usace-shallow-land-disposal-area.st: site maintenance, monitoring, and security ongoing; remediation funded for 2026
fusrap-usace-shallow-land-disposal-area.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — site maintenance, monitoring, and security ongoing; remediation funded for 2026. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report: Congress added the site in 2002 and assigned cleanup to the USACE Pittsburgh District; USACE is maintaining the site, conducting regular environmental monitoring, and providing security; trench excavation was anticipated to begin in summer 2025 and remediation work in late 2025. A Dec. 4, 2025 USACE release provided $32.4 million for site remediation, operation and maintenance, and site security activities in 2026. Official USACE project page was moved (page updated June 16, 2026) to the Pittsburgh / LRD SLDA site. Still on the official list of 20 active USACE sites pending transfer to DOE LM.
fig: Contaminants

Radioactive nuclear wastes from the nearby Nuclear Materials and Equipment Corporation (NUMEC) site, disposed in 10 trenches (about 1.2 acres) in the 1960s and 1970s; materials produced primarily for fuel for nuclear-powered submarines and power plants

fusrap-usace-superior-steel.st: Record of Decision issued August 10, 2026, concluding that no action is necessary to protect human health and the environment from FUSRAP materials
fusrap-usace-superior-steel.what: Active USACE FUSRAP site — Record of Decision issued August 10, 2026, concluding that no action is necessary to protect human health and the environment from FUSRAP materials. Official June 2025 Stakeholder Report had said a No Further Action ROD was expected in FY 2025 after a 2022 RI. The site has not transferred to DOE LM and remains on the official list of 20 active USACE FUSRAP sites. It is not a completed/transferred LM site.
fig: Contaminants
Uranium (natural and enriched; recycled uranium from reprocessed spent fuel may also have been processed) and thorium metal (licensed 1957–1958 for processing and shaping)
